correctness.rationale: The discrete chain B_{k+1}=B_k+1 or 2(B_k+1) with respective probabilities B_k/(B_k+1) and 1/(B_k+1) is exact. For Y_k=B_k/k the nonroot update equals flow Φ_Δ(z)=1+(z−1)e^(−Δ); first-jump hazard ∫0^Δ ds/Φ_s(z)=log(1+1/(kz)) makes its Bernoulli probability exactly 1/(kz+1). Subsequent multiple-jump discrepancies have expected O(k^(−2)) cost, giving the stated finite logarithmic-horizon coupling bound. The PDMP Lyapunov drift L(1+z)=3−(1+z), and one-jump density minorization on compact sets yield unique attracting invariant law via standard Harris theory; combined with mean E Y_k=2/tightness this yields full weak convergence. Generator L z^r=(r−1+2^r)z^(r−1)−r z^r matches the known moment recurrence. Independently verified exact generator/hazard identities and bounded chain moments. Full general proof relies on stated small-set/aperiodicity verification, not simulations.
residual_risks: Full Harris theorem assumptions rely on a common one-jump density, not finite simulated moments; inspected proof gives suitable compact minorization.
